title: C482/417/2005 of SANU TANDON Vs STATE AND ANOTHER

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Recall / Restoration Appn. 278 of 2010
Compounding Appn. No. 409 / 2010
In
Crl. Misc. Application (C-482) No. 417 of 2005
Sanu Tandon
S/o Late Shyam Narayan Tandon
R/o Lal Kurti, Ishwar Nagar,
Near Amar Ujala Press, Agra.
................ Petitioner
Versus
1. State of Uttaranchal
2. Pooja D/o Sri Prem Nath Kapoor
R/o Upper Bazar, Sri Nagar (Garhwal),
Uttaranchal.
................ Respondents
Mr. Subhash Chandra Tyagi, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mrs. Mamta Bisht, A.G.A. for respondent No. 1 / State.
Mr. Rajendra Singh, Advocate for respondent No. 2 / complainant.
Hon'ble Prafulla C. Pant, J.
This is Recall / Restoration MCRC Application No.
278 of 2010, moved on behalf of the petitioner, for
restoration of Criminal Misc. Application (C-482) No.
417 of 2005, which was dismissed for non-prosecution on
22.04.2009.

2
The application is accompanied with Delay
Condonation Application No. 408 of 2010 and the
affidavit.
2) Heard.
3) The Delay condonation application is allowed.
Delay is condoned.
4) Also, Recall / Restoration MCRC Application No.
278 of 2010 is allowed.
5) The petition under Section 482 of the Code of
Criminal Procedure, 1973 (for short Cr.P.C.) is restored
to its original number on the condition that parties shall
argue the case, today itself.
6) Also, heard on the petition moved under Section
482 of Cr.P.C.
7) Learned counsel for the parties submitted that
parties to the matrimony have entered into compromise.
They further state that Sanu Tandon (husband) and Pooja
(respondent No. 2) are present in person in the Court.
The two verified the compromise filed before this Court
today. The compromise is supported by affidavit filed by
complainant Pooja. It is stated by her that now she is
peacefully living with her husband and does not want to
prosecute the petitioner.

3
8) Therefore, in view of the principle of law laid down
in B.S. Joshi Vs. State of Haryana, (2003) 4 Supreme
Court Cases 675, the petition under Section 482 of
Cr.P.C. deserves to be allowed.
9) Therefore, the petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C.
is allowed. The proceedings of Criminal Case No. 281 of
2005; State Vs. Sanu Tandon and others, relating to
offence punishable under Section 498-A, 323, 504, 506
of I.P.C., and one punishable under Section 3/4 of the
Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, pending in the court of
Judicial Magistrate First Class, Srinagar (Garhwal), are
hereby quashed. (Compounding Application No. 409 of
2010 also stands disposed of).
(Prafulla C. Pant, J.)
Dt. April 28, 2010.
H. Negi
